Chapter 31

The landing page and the prerendered templates

A prerendered landing page with a GSAP entrance behind an attachment and hydratable random dots, and template pages prerendered from entries() with their formulas already computed on the server.

By the end of this chapter

Prerender pages that have dynamic parameters, animate an entrance without blanking the page, and use hydratable for a value the server and client must agree on.

Why the drifting dots use hydratable

The hero has eighteen dots at random positions. Render them on the server and the browser would render eighteen different random positions during hydration, and Svelte would find the markup did not match. hydratable(key, fn) runs the function on the server, serialises the result into the page, and hands the browser the same value under the same key. The random numbers are computed once, and hydration finds what it expects.

The demo’s numbers live in a module, beside the inputs that produce them. The page draws them as text and never loads the engine to show five rows; the first version had the three totals written into a nested ternary on the column index, inside the markup, and a comment claiming a test computed them. None did.

Now one does. The spec loads the demo’s inputs into the real engine and checks every answer the page shows — and checks that DEMO_RESULTS names exactly the formula cells, so a formula added without its answer, or an answer left behind after its formula went, fails here rather than on the landing page.

The entrance is an attachment, so the markup says {@attach cinematic()} and nothing else; the elements it moves are marked in the hero with data-word, data-pad and data-rise, and the attachment finds them with querySelectorAll. GSAP is imported dynamically inside it so its sixty kilobytes never reach anyone who does not see the animation; prefersReducedMotion is checked first; and nothing in the stylesheet starts at opacity: 0, so a failed import leaves the page visible. Restraint is the design: one timeline, a second long.

Templates from entries

A dynamic route cannot be prerendered unless SvelteKit knows its parameters; entries lists them, and the list is the same array the templates module exports, so adding a template adds a page. The load runs the engine — on the build machine — and the page arrives with the numbers in it.

Two ways in: a local copy with no account, or — if whoAmI() says somebody is signed in — a form that saves the template into the account. The form is create from chapter 27 with two hidden fields. The link is the way in that needs no JavaScript; the save button arrives with it, and the comment above the boundary says why.

Why the save button is not in the prerendered page

The page is prerendered: built once, on the build machine, for nobody in particular. There is no person to ask about at build time, and an answer baked into the file would be the build machine’s — nobody — served to everybody. The empty pending snippet is how the page says so. On the server, a boundary with a pending snippet renders that snippet and skips its content, so the build neither awaits whoAmI() nor writes a stranger’s answer into the HTML; the built file has no “Save to my account” in it at all. In the browser, the content renders once the answer arrives, and the form appears only for somebody signed in. An earlier draft of this chapter said the form worked with JavaScript off. It cannot, because it is not in the page until JavaScript has asked who you are; the no-script path is the link beside it, which needs neither.

Checkpoint

  • You can say what would go wrong if the dots used Math.random() directly.
  • You can explain why entries returns the template slugs and not a hard-coded list.
  • You can say why <svelte:element this={…}> is used for the section heading.
